perItem.how: AppInfo::refreshComponents no longer uses waitForFinished. It starts one QProcess per tool (yt-dlp, FFmpeg, Deno) in parallel through askVersion(). Each process settles exactly once, through finished or through errorOccurred(FailedToStart). A per-process QTimer kills it after 20 s; the old 4 s limit was too short for a cold yt-dlp start under emulation. publishComponents() builds the list when the last answer arrives. A round counter makes a newer read (for example after a tool update) discard an older one, and a pending token stops a tool that fails to start at once from publishing before the others are asked. copyReport() never blocks: if versions are not known yet it sets m_copyWhenKnown and copies once they arrive. Main.qml now builds SettingsView through a Loader that becomes active the first time Settings is shown and then stays built. The ViewFade latches `opened` on any change of `shown`, which avoids the binding loop an onLoaded latch caused. The 'Reading versions…' label shows until the answers arrive.

Added PlaybackController::restoreSettings(). main.cpp calls it right after setLibrary() and before loadModel() and QML load. It reads player.volume, player.shuffle, player.repeat and player.autoplay from the settings table through Library::settingValue, writing the members directly so setShuffle does not shuffle an empty queue or write the value back. Unset or unreadable values keep their defaults. Values are written through Library::setSetting when they change: setShuffle, cycleRepeat and setAutoplay write immediately. setVolume restarts a 400 ms single-shot timer so a slider drag makes one write, not dozens; a still-pending volume write is also flushed on aboutToQuit. A shuffle left on shuffles the startup queue, as it would have in the last session.

DownloadManager's available and canConvert are now NOTIFY toolsChanged instead of CONSTANT. New refreshTools() (Q_INVOKABLE) looks for yt-dlp (YtDlp::isAvailable) and FFmpeg (YtDlp::ffmpegPath) again and emits only when something changed. AppInfo has a new toolsUpdated() signal, emitted whenever the setup-script process finishes, whatever the exit code, because a partly failed run may still have installed some tools. main.cpp connects it to downloads.refreshTools. enqueue() also re-checks lazily: at most once every 3 s, so 'Download all' over an album does not search PATH per track, and it re-checks before refusing when yt-dlp was missing.

perItem.how: PlaybackController::beginTrack now calls MpvEngine::stop() as soon as a new track begins, so the old song stops before the new one resolves. MpvEngine numbers each loadfile, passing the number as reply_userdata. When MPV_EVENT_COMMAND_REPLY arrives for the latest load, the engine reads playlist_entry_id from the reply. If the reply has no id, it takes the next START_FILE's entry instead. START_FILE records which entry is running. END_FILE (EOF or error) is passed on only when its playlist_entry_id is the current entry. Position, duration, picture size and metadata are passed on only after the current entry has started. Pause and buffering are still passed on as before. stop() and load() both clear the current entry, and stop() also clears the engine's duration and picture size, so nothing from a replaced or stopped file (its clock, its end, its error, or a late loadfile answer) reaches the new track. The position reads 0:00 until the new file reports time. A loadfile that mpv rejects in its reply now emits loadFailed instead of failing silently. No changes to the tier ladder, itag selection, prefetch or skip-after-failure logic.

beginTrack sets a new m_listenPending flag. The new startListening() writes history, Recently played and the play event exactly once, then emits a new playRecorded signal. It runs immediately for tracks started with autoplay, and from play() for a track that was only loaded (the launch track, or one reached with Next or Previous while paused). main.cpp now reloads Catalog::reloadRecent and Library::reloadHistory on playRecorded instead of currentTrackChanged. play() now sets m_autoPlayAfterResolve, so Play pressed while the track is still resolving starts it when it arrives. pause() clears that flag. mpv now starts with pause=yes, which matches MpvEngine::m_paused, so the launch track does not read as playing while it resolves. Resolve failures, the final mpv load failure and 'No playable source' now emit playbackError (the toast) only when the listener was waiting for sound. Otherwise they update the status line only. If the current track is showing an error, Play retries it as a requested track, and a second failure produces the toast.

perItem.how: InnerTube's m_search/m_suggest/m_radio are now a private Slot {QPointer<QNetworkReply> reply; quint64 generation}. A new static release(Slot&) bumps the generation and then aborts the reply. search, searchYouTube, suggest, radio (through cancelRadio) and all three cancel* calls use it. send() records the slot's generation when it starts. The finished handler, the 1.2 s retry lambda and the 400 region-rejection resend (after g_regionRejected runs) all check a `superseded()` lambda and drop themselves if the generation has moved on. So an old retry can no longer put itself back into the slot and silence a newer search or radio request.

MediaExtractor::search now calls setLastError(QString()) before the empty-query early return. SearchView's error Text also needs root.term.length > 0, so the old error doesn't show during the 250 ms debounce either.

TopBar.focusSearch() calls forceActiveFocus() and selectAll(). TopBar.clearSearch() stops the suggest timer, resets suggesting and highlighted, empties the text, calls Extractor.clearSuggestions() and puts focus back in the field. The clear control is an IconButton('x') inside the search box: visible only when there is text, iconColor Theme.neutral700 (so it turns ink on hover through IconButton), no plate, side 28 with padding Theme.space1 so the cross is 10 px. The TextInput's right edge anchors to it. Main.qml has a new openSearch(), which closes Now Playing, navigates to search and calls topBar.focusSearch(). The Find shortcut and both sidebars (docked and overlay) use it when the view is 'search'. Typing still goes through navigate() and does not select all.

Catalog now has m_refreshQueued. refresh() sets it and returns when m_pendingHome > 0. While it is set, both browse callbacks skip applying their stale answer and only count down. finishHome() takes the flag with std::exchange and calls refresh() before publishing or scheduling a retry, so Home stays 'loading' until the new country's answer arrives.

perItem.how: ~Recommender now calls m_thread.requestInterruption(), quit(), then wait() with no timeout (it used to be wait(2000)). A new Rec::stopRequested() in shelves.h/.cpp wraps QThread::currentThread()->isInterruptionRequested(). The shelf builders check it between scans and return early: the song-shelf loop, before the taste and recent scans, the liked-artist loop, the cold-start shelf, and the start of buildRegionShelves plus each of its 28 per-artist graph reads. RecommenderWorker::build checks it at the start, before the region shelves and before emitting, so a page cut short is never sent. load() skips itself if a stop is already requested. The stop is also checked inside the two long one-time index builds, and a stopped index is thrown away rather than kept half-built. Catalog::ensureArtistIndex checks every 4096 artists/rows; it took about 1.9 s of the old wait. Graph::buildNameIndex checks between shards, and findArtist does not cache a miss caused by a stop. Main-thread callers (the self-tests) are unaffected because nobody interrupts that thread.

New Rec::likedSongs(events) in taste.h/.cpp: each song's newest like or unlike decides, keyed by strictKey. buildTaste counts a like only if the song is liked now, and only the newest like, so a song liked twice votes once. likedArtists in shelves.cpp now uses the same helper instead of its own copy of the rule. The 'More like X' song shelves are seeded only by plays that said yes: the song is liked now, or the label is 0.6 or higher, or the play is unlabelled and was heard for at least 30 s. isWeekend uses when.toLocalTime().date(). --rec-test in main.cpp gains checks for all three.

reviews.checked: Read AGENT_BRIEF.md and p12_items.json. Went through the whole diff 130614b..HEAD for Monolist Player (5 commits) and the code around each change: playbackcontroller.cpp/h in full, mpvengine.cpp/h in full, mpvengine_stub.cpp, innertube.cpp send/release/search/suggest/radio, mediaextractor.cpp search/cancel, catalog.cpp in full, appinfo.cpp components and tool update, downloadmanager.cpp/h, ytdlp.cpp tool lookup, recommender.cpp worker/destructor, rec/taste.cpp, rec/shelves.cpp buildShelves and likedArtists, rec/catalog.cpp ensureArtistIndex, rec/graph.cpp findArtist, Main.qml, TopBar.qml, SearchView.qml, SettingsView.qml, NowPlayingBar.qml, TrackMenu.qml, MonoMenuItem.qml, Sidebar.qml, NowPlayingView.qml pane, Library settingValue/setSetting/dropRegion, and the QML callers of Downloads.available/enqueue. Checked mpv event ordering against the bundled libmpv client.h: property changes are coalesced and delivered only after queued events, so START_FILE and COMMAND_REPLY are always handled before the new file's time-pos and duration, and the entry filtering drops nothing from the new file. Ran the built Debug exe with a scratch MONOLIST_DATA_DIR: `monolist.exe --rec-test Z:\Desktop\AryaMusix\musicplayer\EmbeddingData`. The B11 checks pass: re-liked counts, liked twice counts once, unliked counts 0; song shelves are Levitating | Creep | Yellow; weekend mass 2.00 vs 0.00. Traced these flows by reading the code: first-run settings restore (empty table keeps defaults), the save paths, next/previous/gapless EOF, RepeatOne, seek, the tier ladder and cache refresh, skip-after-failure, the autoplay radio wait, the search/suggest/radio generation handling including the 400 region resend, Home refresh queuing including region rejection, the version-read rounds and copy-when-known, the recommender stop checks and wait(), and the like/unlike rules. These looked correct; the four findings are the problems I found. The m_playing desync (finding 1) was not reproduced at runtime, because it needs a resolve that fails and then succeeds on retry, which the existing self-tests cannot stage. It follows directly from the code, and a comment in handleResolveFailed already describes the same effect (no pause change, so the flag is never set back).

findings.problem: The new retry in play() can leave the player unable to pause. When a track fails for good, handleResolveFailed (line 864) and the final loadFailed branch (line 126) call setPlayingFlag(false) but do not pause mpv. Since B05, beginTrack has already stopped the old file, so mpv sits idle with pause=no. The retry then succeeds and load(url, true) calls setPaused(false). mpv's pause does not change, so no pausedChanged arrives and m_playing stays false while the song plays. togglePlay() keeps going to play(), which only unpauses, so neither the Play button nor Space can pause it. When the song ends, next() sees m_playing false and loads the following track paused, so the queue stops.
findings.scenario: Listen to a playlist. The network drops, three tracks in a row fail to resolve, and the status reads 'Nothing here will play' (or: a last-in-queue track fails with no upcoming track). mpv is idle, unpaused, with m_playing false. The network comes back and the user presses Play. The retry resolves and the song plays, but the bar shows a Play icon. Pressing it or Space does nothing, and at the end of the song the next track loads paused. The same desync happens on the older path where the user double-clicks another song after the failure; the new Play retry makes it the main recovery flow.
findings.fix: Keep the flag and mpv in agreement at the terminal failures: in the non-skip branch of handleResolveFailed and the final branch of the loadFailed handler, call m_engine->setPaused(true) (the flag then follows through pausedChanged) instead of only setPlayingFlag(false). Alternatively, pause the engine at the start of play()'s m_statusError branch before beginCurrent(true), so the later setPaused(false) is a real change.

findings.problem: The lazy re-check added for B13 can never switch downloads back on. It runs only inside enqueue(), but every control that calls enqueue is hidden or disabled while Downloads.available is false: DownloadButton (visible: ... && Downloads.available), the TrackMenu 'Download' item (enabled: Downloads.available ...), and the PlaylistView/PageView 'Download all' (visible: Downloads.available). So when yt-dlp was missing at launch, the only thing that re-checks is AppInfo::toolsUpdated, which comes from Settings > Update components. The app's own instructions point elsewhere: the DownloadsView note says 'Run scripts\setup-windows.ps1, or place yt-dlp next to the app', and main.cpp logs 'Install with pip install yt-dlp'. Tools installed any of those ways stay unused until a restart, which is exactly the B13 complaint.
findings.scenario: Start the app with no yt-dlp. Downloads shows the 'Downloading needs yt-dlp' note and every download control is hidden. In a terminal, run setup-windows.ps1 or pip install yt-dlp, then come back to the app. Nothing calls refreshTools(), available stays false, and the controls stay hidden until the app is restarted.
findings.fix: Re-check from a place the user can reach while the tools are missing. For example, call Downloads.refreshTools() when DownloadsView becomes visible or the window is re-activated while !Downloads.available, or re-check on Qt.application.state becoming Active. refreshTools is already Q_INVOKABLE and emits toolsChanged only when something changed, so it is cheap.

findings.problem: next() and previous() still treat m_resolving as 'was playing': advance(m_playing || m_resolving) at line 958 and wasPlaying = m_playing || m_resolving at line 1001. After B04, a track can be resolving without anyone wanting sound: the launch track (loadModel, autoPlay=false), or a track reached with Next while paused. Pressing Next again during that resolve goes to playIndex, which starts playback and records history and a play event. This breaks B04's promise that tracks reached with Next while paused load paused and are recorded only on Play. With the network down it also runs the skip-and-toast chain the fix meant to keep quiet.
findings.scenario: Pause, then press Next twice quickly (Ctrl+Right twice); the first press loads track B paused and 'Resolving source…' shows. The second press sees m_resolving true, playIndex(C) starts C playing although the user was paused, and C is written to History, Recently played and play_events. The same thing happens pressing Next during the launch track's resolve. Offline, C then fails, skips and ends in an error toast.
findings.fix: Use the flag this batch already defines as 'the listener is waiting for sound': keepPlaying = m_playing || (m_resolving && m_autoPlayAfterResolve) in next(), and the same expression for wasPlaying in previous().

findings.problem: The new Play-on-error retry (beginCurrent(true)) writes a listen before anything has played. beginTrack(autoPlay=true) calls startListening() at once (line 747), so each Play press on a failed track adds a history row, bumps play_count in 'recent', and opens a play_event. That event closes with listened 0, i.e. label 0.0, which buildTaste counts as a negative vote. If the retry fails again, the skip chain (up to three tracks) records each skipped track the same way. Before this batch, Play on a failed track recorded nothing. The lens asks for no records of tracks never heard, and B04's done line says a paused-loaded track is recorded when it starts playing.
findings.scenario: Launch offline. The launch track fails quietly, as intended. The user presses Play two or three times while still offline. Each press adds History and Recently played entries plus label-0.0 play_events for that track and up to two skipped tracks after it. None of them made a sound, yet they now appear in Recently played and push the taste profile away from songs the listener chose.
findings.fix: Record the listen when the engine actually starts the file rather than when the retry is requested. For example, keep m_listenPending set through the retry and call startListening() from handleResolved (or on the first positionChanged after the file starts) when m_autoPlayAfterResolve is true. Or at least drop the play event (skip closePlayEvent's label) when the resolve for it fails.

reviews.checked:
I read the brief, p12_items.json and the full diff 130614b..HEAD (commits a70ea55, befc3e5, ece98af, 3da36b6, 83c0313), plus the surrounding code in appinfo.cpp (updateTools included), mpvengine.cpp (all of it), playbackcontroller.cpp (constructor, beginTrack, resolve handlers, play and pause, advance), recommender.cpp (worker, ctor/dtor, refresh), rec/catalog.cpp (ensureArtistIndex and its mutex callers), rec/graph.cpp (buildNameIndex, findArtist), innertube.cpp (send, release, withVisitorData, all slot users), catalog.cpp, ytdlp.cpp (locate and findTool, which have no cache), the destruction order of the stack objects in main.cpp, and the QML users of Downloads.available and TrackMenu.

Lifetime points I checked and found sound:
- AppInfo askVersion settles each process exactly once. The version processes, their timeout timers and the settle connections (with AppInfo as context) are torn down safely at quit: ~QObject disconnects the handlers before ~QProcess kills a child. Rounds discard stale answers, and a synchronous FailedToStart during start() is covered by the pending token.
- The mpv loadfile reply is always queued before that file's START_FILE. END_FILE and per-file properties are gated on playlist_entry_id, stop() uses userdata 0 and moves the load number on, and no other async commands collide with the numbering.
- The InnerTube generation token covers the retry timer, the 400 resend and abort-while-finishing. All three slots call release() first.
- The recommender worker is deleted on its own thread through finished→deleteLater. The interruption flag is atomic, the artist index is built under m_artistMutex, the graph stays on one thread, the worker makes no blocking cross-thread calls, and all DB access stays on the main thread.
- The TrackMenu is a single instance per TrackTable, not a per-delegate object.

I ran the built Debug exe (22:50 build) three times against a scratch MONOLIST_DATA_DIR with rec.dataDir and rec.graphDir set, using '--view settings --play LrM_Y39Gmhk 1|4'. Each run quit while the version checks and the first recommendations build could still be in progress. All runs exited cleanly in 1.9–5.2 s, with no qFatal and no 'QProcess destroyed while running' warning. I edited, built and committed nothing.

findings.problem: The B13 lazy re-check in enqueue() can never help when yt-dlp was missing at launch, because nothing in the UI calls enqueue() while Downloads.available is false. Every entry point is hidden or disabled on that property: DownloadButton.qml:30 (visible), TrackMenu.qml:57 (enabled), the 'Download all' buttons in PlaylistView.qml:251 and PageView.qml:154 (visible), TrackTable's download column and NowPlayingBar.qml:131. The only other path is AppInfo::toolsUpdated, which only the Windows setup script emits. AppInfo::setupScriptPath() returns empty outside Q_OS_WIN, so on macOS canUpdateTools is false and toolsUpdated never fires. A tool installed outside the app is therefore never noticed until restart. This is outside the lifetime lens but fails B13's done line ('lazily on enqueue … new tools work without a restart').
findings.scenario: Launch without yt-dlp: downloads are disabled and the startup log says to run `pip install yt-dlp`. With the app still running, run `pip install yt-dlp` or `brew install yt-dlp`, or drop yt-dlp into tools/. The download buttons stay hidden and the menu item stays greyed, so enqueue() is never reached and refreshTools() never runs. On macOS 'Update components' is disabled, so no path picks the tool up. Downloads stay off until restart.
findings.fix: Re-check without needing an enqueue: call Downloads.refreshTools() when the Downloads view or the track menu opens (it is cheap, and the 3 s throttle could live in refreshTools itself), and/or on application focus-in or a slow timer while !m_available. Keep the enqueue check for the case where a tool was removed.

findings.problem: copyReport() before the versions are in now defers the clipboard write until every --version process answers. That can be up to kVersionTimeoutMs = 20 s later (yt-dlp's cold Python start is exactly the slow one). The write gives no feedback and has no cancel, so the pending copy outlives the user's intent and overwrites whatever they have put on the clipboard since.
findings.scenario: Open Settings for the first time, which starts refreshComponents(). Yt-dlp takes several seconds to answer under emulation, or hangs until the 20 s kill. Scroll to 07 About and click 'COPY FOR A BUG REPORT →' while 'Reading versions…' still shows: nothing is copied yet. Switch to a browser and copy a URL. When the last version answers, publishComponents() runs copyReport() and silently replaces the URL with the report, so the next paste is the wrong text.
findings.fix: Either copy at once with whatever is known (versions shown as 'reading…') and re-copy only if the clipboard still holds that first report, or disable the action while !About.componentsKnown. If the deferral stays, drop it when the clipboard changes in the meantime (QClipboard::dataChanged) or after a short limit.

findings.problem: ~Recommender now calls m_thread.wait() with no timeout. The stop checks sit between scans, and the reads between them go to the catalogue (mmap) and the graph shards (SQLite), which can live on a network share. If that share stalls, a read page-faulting into it or a shard query can block well beyond one scan. The GUI thread then waits indefinitely at exit after the QML engine and window are gone. The old code crashed after 2 s; this code can leave a windowless process running.
findings.scenario: The catalogue and GraphData are on an SMB or psf share, as the code comments anticipate. A first build is inside buildNameIndex's per-shard SELECT or the first topK scan when the share drops (Wi-Fi lost, VM share suspended), and the user quits. The window closes, and main() blocks in ~Recommender until the SMB timeout expires, or much longer on a hard mount. On macOS, clicking the Dock icon during that time activates the dead instance instead of starting a new one, so the app appears not to open.
findings.fix: Keep the interruption, but bound the join: wait(QDeadlineTimer(10000)). If the thread is still running, log it and deliberately leak the QThread and the worker (heap-allocate m_thread and do not destroy it), so there is neither a qFatal nor an unbounded hang, and let process exit reclaim it.

reviews.checked:
Read the brief, p12_items.json and the full diff 130614b..HEAD for Monolist Player (5 commits: a70ea55, befc3e5, ece98af, 3da36b6, 83c0313), and saved it to scratchpad/port_src.diff and port_qml.diff.

Platform guards: no new Windows-only API, .exe name, backslash path or WinAPI in any changed C++ or QML line. Qt minimum: CMake requires Qt 6.6 (qt_standard_project_setup REQUIRES 6.5). The MONOLIST_NO_MPV stub still defines stop(), which beginTrack now calls, so the new call adds no link break; the stub's existing mismatches are ROADMAP M04.

I ran mingw g++ -fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra with the build's own defines and includes on the 13 changed .cpp files: appinfo, catalog, downloadmanager, innertube, mediaextractor, mpvengine, playbackcontroller, rec/catalog, rec/graph, rec/shelves, rec/taste, recommender, main. findings.problem: B13's lazy re-check can never run in the one case it exists for. enqueue() only calls refreshTools() when something calls enqueue(), and every UI path to enqueue is hidden or disabled while Downloads.available is false: DownloadButton.qml:30, TrackMenu.qml:57, PageView.qml:154, PlaylistView.qml:251 and NowPlayingBar.qml:131. That needs setupScriptPath(), which returns empty outside Q_OS_WIN (appinfo.cpp:344-353), and on Windows it also returns empty when the script is not next to the build. So on macOS/Linux nothing ever re-checks a missing yt-dlp, and the done line's 'so new tools work without a restart' fails there. The same happens on Windows whenever tools are installed any way other than the Settings button.
findings.scenario: Windows machine with no yt-dlp in tools\ and no python/python3 on PATH, so Downloads.available is false. The Downloads page says 'Downloading needs yt-dlp. Run scripts\setup-windows.ps1, or place yt-dlp next to the app.' The user copies yt-dlp.exe next to monolist.exe while the app runs, as told. No Download button, menu item or 'Download all' ever appears, because enqueue() is never reachable, so refreshTools() never runs. It still needs a restart. On macOS/Linux, `brew install yt-dlp` or `pacman -S yt-dlp` hits the same dead end in any setup where available was false (and M03's fix to the python fallback will make that the common case). Caveat: today any python3 on PATH makes available true (ROADMAP M03), which hides this on most machines. canConvert does refresh lazily, because the buttons stay visible then.
findings.fix: Give the re-check a trigger the UI can reach while downloads are unavailable. For example, call Downloads.refreshTools() when DownloadsView becomes visible and when the window becomes active again (Qt.application.state === Qt.ApplicationActive). Or keep the Download entry enabled when !available and let enqueue() re-check before it refuses. refreshTools() is already rate-limited and cheap: a PATH lookup.

outcomes.finding: playbackcontroller.cpp:930 (major): after a final failure, the new Play retry leaves m_playing false while mpv plays, so the song can't be paused
outcomes.why: Reproduced before the fix with the new --queue-test <good> --recover <bad> script. After the broken song failed, the good song played again but showed 'paused', and Play/Pause let the clock run 1020 ms in a second. Added PlaybackController::haltPlayback(), which clears the flag and also pauses mpv. It now runs at the terminal failure in handleResolveFailed, at the final loadFailed branch, and at the two radio 'End of the queue' branches, which had the same desync. After the fix the test shows 'good again ... playing', then 'paused' with the clock moving 0 ms.

outcomes.finding: downloadmanager.cpp:174 (major, correctness): B13's re-check on enqueue can never switch downloads on, because every enqueue control is hidden while !available
outcomes.why: Confirmed by grep: DownloadButton, TrackMenu, PageView/PlaylistView 'Download all', TrackTable and NowPlayingBar all depend on Downloads.available. Added DownloadManager::refreshToolsIfStale(), a Q_INVOKABLE that re-checks at most once every 3 s. It runs from enqueue, from QGuiApplication::applicationStateChanged when the window becomes active (wired in main.cpp), and from DownloadsView.onVisibleChanged. refreshTools() still runs unthrottled on toolsUpdated. outcomes.why: Reproduced before the fix: paused, then two quick Nexts ended on 'Recover test 3 ... playing', with one more play and one more event recorded. next() and previous() now use m_playing || (m_resolving && m_autoPlayAfterResolve). outcomes.finding: appinfo.cpp:256 (minor): copyReport before the versions arrive writes the clipboard up to 20 s later, over whatever was copied since
outcomes.why: Confirmed in the code: the copy was deferred until publishComponents. copyReport() now copies at once. Before the versions are read, report() lists Qt and says 'other components: versions not read yet'. When they arrive, publishComponents swaps in the full report only if the clipboard still holds that first text, compared without \r. Checked by build and by reading the code only; no runtime clipboard test.

outcomes.finding: recommender.cpp:344 (minor, low confidence): ~Recommender waits with no timeout, so a stalled network share could hang exit
outcomes.why: B10's done line asks for exactly this: the destructor waits until the worker stops, and the worker checks for interruption between scans. The proposed bounded wait plus leaked thread doesn't help. A thread blocked in paging or SMB I/O keeps the process alive during teardown on both Windows and macOS anyway. A leaked worker still running against its catalogue and QtSql shard connections while statics are destroyed would turn a slow exit into a crash. No change made.
